Optimal.Notes: FSR Balanced at 1024x640 internal resolution offers a noticeably sharper image than Performance mode while still keeping the GPU within reach of 30 fps in most areas; expect drops in dense combat or open vistas. GE-Proton is recommended by ProtonDB reporters for best compatibility with this title.

profiles.Summary: Black Myth: Wukong is a visually demanding Unreal Engine 5 action RPG that significantly exceeds the Steam Deck's GPU capabilities, requiring aggressive upscaling and low settings to reach a playable 30 fps. It is officially unsupported on Deck but runs under Proton with some effort, and FSR is essential to reach even a modest frame rate target.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available — these profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1060 6GB, well above the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti GPU) and the game's UE5 engine demands. On your first run, check frame rate in the opening area and in combat; if you see consistent drops below 25 fps, drop to the Max Battery profile and reduce FSR mode to Performance.

MaxBattery.Notes: Set the in-game upscaling to FSR Performance and render at 960x600 to maximise GPU headroom; even so, this is a very GPU-heavy UE5 title and battery life will be short. The 40 Hz refresh rate with a 30 fps cap reduces screen tearing and slightly eases GPU load.

KnownIssues: Game is officially Steam Deck Unsupported — some menus and cutscenes may have input or display issues
UE5 Lumen and Nanite features are extremely demanding and must be disabled or minimised
Shader compilation stutters are expected on first launch and in new areas
High VRAM pressure from shared 16 GB pool may cause frame pacing issues at higher resolutions

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at native 1280x800 with FSR Quality is the best visual fidelity the Deck can attempt, but the GPU will be fully saturated and frame rate may dip below 30 fps in demanding scenes — a hard 30 fps cap prevents runaway frame pacing. Battery life will be very short at full 15 W TDP.

Optimal.Notes: A 30 fps cap with FSR Balanced at 1024x640 internal provides a reasonable balance of visual fidelity and stability; shadows and foliage at medium add noticeable detail without breaking the budget. Expect brief dips during large boss fights.

On first launch, run the in-game benchmark or play the opening area and check the frame-rate overlay — if you're consistently below 25 fps even in MaxBattery mode, lower the upscaling quality to Ultra Performance and reduce shadow quality to Low.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 with FSR Performance upscaling to give the GPU headroom under an 8 W TDP cap; image quality will be soft but the game remains playable. Drop to 6 W TDP if the device runs hot.

UE5 Lumen and Nanite features are extremely GPU-heavy and should be disabled or set to minimum on Deck

No native Linux build — runs via Proton with gold-tier reliability; some cutscene or audio desync issues reported

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at 40 Hz/40 fps with the GPU and TDP at their maximums extracts the most from the Deck OLED; the 40 fps cap feels smooth on the OLED panel and avoids the tearing of an uncapped run. Battery life will be short — keep a charger handy.
